title: Parent user identifiable from registration data
description: The registration flow transmits personally identifiable information (email, name, government ID) that directly identifies the parent user, making them identifiable to the authentication service and any party that accesses this data.
assumptions: Standard registration flow with PII collection

title: Sensitive registration data disclosure
description: The authentication service receives sensitive data (password, government ID, six-digit code) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure storage, transmission, or access controls.
assumptions: Data stored or processed by authentication service

title: Registration data aggregation with other user data
description: The authentication service could aggregate this registration data with other data about the parent user (e.g., usage patterns, other accounts), creating a more comprehensive profile than the user intended.
assumptions: Authentication service has access to or can link with other data sources

title: Parent unaware of data collection scope
description: The parent user may not be fully aware of what data is being collected, how it will be used, stored, or shared with third parties during the registration process.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not be clear or user may not read it

title: Registration data sent to unintended recipients
description: The registration data could be forwarded to or accessed by unintended recipients (e.g., third-party services, other system components) without the parent user's explicit consent.
assumptions: System architecture may include data sharing with external parties

title: Unauthorized access to stored parent account data
description: The Authentication Service stores parent account information in MongoDB. If access controls are insufficient or the database is compromised, unauthorized parties could access sensitive parent account data including authentication credentials and user information.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has standard security configuration; parent account data includes PII or authentication-sensitive information

title: Excessive data collection for parent accounts
description: The Authentication Service may store more parent account data than necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles. This could include unnecessary personal identifiers or metadata that enable profiling.
assumptions: Parent account storage includes fields beyond strict authentication requirements

title: Users unaware of parent account data storage
description: Users may not be informed that their parent account information is being stored in MongoDB, or what specific data elements are collected and retained. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy policy or consent mechanisms do not clearly disclose parent account data storage practices

title: Non-compliance with data retention requirements

assumptions: No automated data retention policies or deletion mechanisms are in place for parent account data
